ios.desc:
CodeMate is a native code editor for iPhone and iPad, built for editing source code, updating configuration files, and making quick changes away from your desk.

No desktop IDE complexity. Just fast, focused code viewing and editing designed for touch.

Open more than 200 file formats with native syntax highlighting, including Swift, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C/C++, Go, Rust, HTML, CSS, JSON, XML, YAML, and Markdown.

Access files from iCloud Drive, Dropbox, and other storage providers through the Files app.

Key Features:

• Native code viewing and editing on iPhone and iPad
• Syntax highlighting for 200+ file formats
• Multiple tabs and a minimap for navigating long files
• Light and dark themes with adjustable fonts, spacing, and margins
• Line numbers, current-line highlighting, word wrap, and no-word-wrap modes
• Swift symbol list and jump to any line
• HTML preview with linked CSS and JavaScript
• Custom file extension rules
• Share and print source files
• Export polished code snapshots as images
• External keyboard support for convenient code editing
• Preview and validate XML, JSON, and YAML files
• Find and replace in code with plain text and regular expression support
• Markdown preview

CodeMate is made for developers, students, and anyone who wants a focused, portable way to read, learn from, and edit code.

Homebrew... The only Homebrew I know about is http://brew.sh/

1) There is almost definitely an emacs equivalent for iOS

2) Pycharm- Maybe Textastic (https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/textastic-code-editor-for/id383577124?mt=8) or Codemate (https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/codemate-syntax-highlighter/id680609457?mt=8). I'm not an IDE guy (I use Sublime Text), so YMMV.

3) OK so I get it, you're a Python dev. Admittedly, iOS is lacking in doing native app dev (in fact, I just posted something of that nature to this very thread).

4) Java, etc... I wonder if https://c9.io/ would work...

5) MS Office- Haven't used in years, anyway. I use Google Docs for all that.

6) Adobe stuff- Well, iPad Pro has some version of photoshop, I believe... PDF's are rendered natively in iOS (and quite nicely, actually... just like on OS X)... Illustrator?
